    Sources: the food, recipe and tag tables come from the Kyllox fork client extract (original_yaml), not confirmed Nexon original data. Numeric calculations and naming/processing rules were checked against the current restoration server and client code. Fork reconstructions and developer decisions are marked separately in the text.

    What eating food raises, and how cooking changes the numbers, laid out with the exact formulas the game code uses. Per-level values for each food are in the Food list.

    Source grade — the badge next to a value shows its basis. Last changed next to a section title is the public version in which that section's content last changed, and links to Patch history.
    • Original (confirmed) A value taken directly from a row of the extracted original data with no signs of editing, or from the original client code — 4 on this page
    • Estimated A value the restoration filled in because the original data has no field for it (e.g. rules that were server-only) — 13 on this page
    • Changed from original (developer decision) A value that exists in the original but was set differently by developer decision — 3 on this page
    • Unverified Values not yet backed by a source — shown in section titles — 5 on this page

    Last changed on this page: 2026.09.29.5

    #What happens when you eatLast changed 2026.09.24.5

    Using a food plays the eating animation for the Eating time (digestivetime, multiplied by the “Digestibility/Difficult to Digest” tags), and all effects below apply at once when it ends. Walking or being hit while eating cancels it, and the food returns to its original bag slot (movement within 0.75s of starting is ignored). You cannot eat another food while eating.Estimated

    • Energy — latent energy × instant ratio is gained immediately; the rest (latent − instant) is Digested over 300s and comes in gradually.
    • Health·Life·Fatigue — adds the food's field value with tag modifiers applied (Health cannot exceed its max; Life cannot exceed current Health).
    • Full — adds up and can overflow to 1.2× the max of 100 (120); decreases by 0.1 per second.
    • Water — drinks (water) fully restore Thirst and remove the “Thirst” status.
    • Status effect — applies the effect the food carries (Hot Food, Vigor, water, coffee effects …). Tags can overwrite this field (“Hot” → Hot Food).
    • Raw — while the “Raw” tag remains, the raw food status effect is applied. Cooking (cooking recipes) removes the Raw and Wet tags.
    • Stat buff — buffs such as Strength and Dexterity last for the Buff duration. A previous food buff in the same buff slot is removed (see “Buff slots” below).
    • Taste — depending on the taste score, one of “Delicious/Phenomenal Flavor/Horrible/Disgusting” is applied (see “Taste check” below).
    All numbers on this page come from running the exact formulas the game uses when eating. Formula values were measured with the game code's calculator (NCalc), and buff multipliers with the game code's FoodTagRules.ForkBuffScale.

    #Energy·Recovery formulaLast changed 2026.09.24.5

    Instant energy = latent energy′ × clamp(instant ratio′, 0, 1) Digested energy = latent energy′ − instant energy (evenly over 300s) value′ = (data value + Σ incr − Σ decr) × Π ratio (overwritten if a set tag exists) Health += Health′ (+ max Health × health_ratio) Life += Life′ (+ current Health × life_ratio) Buff duration = buff duration′ (300s if the data value is 0)

    Data value are the original formula evaluated at the food's level (performance.txt food), while Tag formulas use the Tag level, not the food level. When several tags touch the same field, additions (incr/decr) are summed and multipliers (ratio) are multiplied. “set” overwrites the value entirely — e.g. Heated sets Max energy buff to 0, so cooking sashimi removes the max energy buff.Original (confirmed)

    Comparison with original measurements (data recorded in code comments): Raw Meat Dumpling Lv53 67 · Lv60 71, Seasoned Dumpling Stone Plate BBQ Lv54 134 — this formula matches to the integer.

    #Buff slots and durationLast changed 2026.09.24.5

    Food buffs go into one of the original's two status effect slots. The food data's effect_container decides which slot, and only Same slot only overwrite each other. So eating a survival food (Cooked Rice, etc.) leaves a Hamburger's stat buff in place. EstimatedOriginal (confirmed)

    Enhanced Ability (food_ability)
    Most foods — 349 species
    Enhanced Survival (food_survival)
    Dutch Coffee, Cooked Rice, Prawn Skewer — 3 species

    Duration = the food data's modifier_effect_time (300s if 0) with tag modifiers applied. “Status Effect Duration +” extends it per level, and the “Removes Status Effects” tag on preserved dishes sets buff values to 0. If the duration is 0 or the food has no buffs, eating it does not clear previous buffs — dried food lets you refill Energy while keeping your buffs.

    #Fork food buff multiplierLast changed 2026.09.24.5

    Developer decision (2026-09-24) — a fork adjustment, not an original data value. Food buffs in the extracted original (late-service build) are too weak, so stat, combat and crafting buffs are multiplied. Energy, recovery, Full, Digestion, and max Energy / max Fatigue buffs are untouched. Changed from original (developer decision)
    Multiplier = min(base correction × processing stage, max(original Lv60 value, 46) ÷ original Lv60 value) Base correction = clamp(20.88 ÷ original Lv60 value, 1, 3) (only the 8 basic stats; combat/crafting buffs use 1) Processing stage = raw/unprocessed 1 / has a cooking property (Heated, etc.) 1.25 / seasoned with spice 1.5 If the original Lv60 value is negative (a deliberate penalty) the multiplier is 1; buffs not in the data (tag-only) use the processing stage only

    Reference point: Seasoned Meat Dumpling Stone Plate BBQ (Lv60, salt) — original Strength 12 × (20.88/12) × 1.5 × salt amplification 1.15 ≈ 36. The multiplier is set once from the food's Original value at Lv60, and the same multiplier applies to every level's value. Spice amplification and tag modifiers are multiplied on top.

    #Recipe(In-place cooking) 28 kindsLast changed 2026.09.27.2

    In-place cooking (original recipes.txt type 1) cooks the food you put in without creating a new item. The result is the original food with Cooking property tag added, and the Raw (raw_food) and Wet (wet) tags removed. When the same cooking property is added again, the levels are Sum, capped at that property's max level. Spice amplification properties take the last spice's level. Different properties all remain.

    Which dish adds which properties at what level is not in the extracted original data (server logic). Levels follow community sources (Inven kimfree summary · Naver dboy80 “Cooking 101” and “Cooking Encyclopedia”), and the property effect formulas are the original tags.txt as-is. Estimated “Boost Umami” is added only when the input is meat or fish Estimated

    #Spice ampLast changed 2026.09.24.5

    Dishes with a spice slot (seasoned grill, spiced drying, spiced smoking, spiced salting) pick the amplification by the Type tag of the spice used. Amplification tags multiply the matching stat buff (original formula ×(1+0.05·level)). Original (confirmed) Levels are Estimated

    Spice typeTopping ampEffectCorresponding item
    Salt saltExtra STR Amplification Lv3, Extra PER Amplification Lv3Strength ×1.15, Perception ×1.15Salt, Rose Salt
    Sugar sugarExtra DEX Amplification Lv2, Extra PER Amplification Lv2, Extra CHA Amplification Lv2Dexterity ×1.1, Perception ×1.1, Charisma ×1.1Sugar, Honey, [Events] Nagitoz, [Events] Kingkong, [Events] Crunky†
    Herb herbExtra STR Amplification Lv2, Extra AGI Amplification Lv2, Extra WIL Amplification Lv2Strength ×1.1, Agility ×1.1, Will ×1.1Herb, Bud, Purple Tulip Flower

    Spices that belong to none of the three types and give no amplification: Chili Pepper, Bell Pepper.

    Preserved dishes (drying, smoking, salting) set buffs to 0 via “Removes Status Effects”, so the amplification from the spiced variants has no actual effect (it multiplies 0).

    #153 food tagsLast changed 2026.09.27.2

    All tags that attach to food and change values (entries in the original tags.txt with required_performance: food). Value columns show the value at tag level 1 / 2 / 3 / 5 / 7 / 9 / 12 (additive = amount added, multiplicative = multiplier). Original (confirmed)

    Food with at least one tag marked “Yes” in the “Cooking property” column gets the fork multiplier's Cooking stage (×1.25); with spice amplification (*_plus_amplifier) it gets the Seasoning stage (×1.5).

    #Processing countLast changed 2026.09.24.5

    Food starts with Processing count 2. In-place cooking recipes that “use 1 processing count” (most of them) consume 1 each time, and at 0 the food can't be cooked further — so a food can be cooked up to twice (e.g. Meat Stone Plate BBQ → Meat Stone Plate BBQ Skewer). Estimated

    • New food made by applied cooking starts with a processing count of 2 by default.
    • Starts at 117 recipes that start with: Bread, Stuffed Bread, Pizza, Cake, Cream Cake, Drip Coffee, Dutch Coffee, Juice, Pressed Grain, Squeezed Oil, Ground Coffee, Rice Puffs, Sausage, Premium Sausage, Sugar, Tea, Fruit Wine.
    • Recipes that use the materials' processing count (original deduct_modifiable_count: Meat Dumpling, Boiled Meat, Aged Cheese) give a result of 1 times if the ingredient was never cooked, 0 times if cooked even once.
    • Aged Cheese can only be made from Cheese that still has processing count left.

    Estimated A rule based on a report (20260923-37) and Naver's “Cooking Encyclopedia”.

    #Material property inheritanceLast changed 2026.09.27.2

    Applied dishes do not inherit ingredients' cooking properties by default. Only the recipes below inherit the cooking properties (Heated, umami, spice amplification …) of the ingredients in the main material slot (base), at the Average(Rounding) of their levels — if only one of three grains was roasted, the average is lower. Estimated

    29 inheriting recipes: Boiled Meat, Bread, Stuffed Bread, Pizza, Cake, Cream Cake, Aged Cheese, Drip Coffee, Dutch Coffee, Bread Dough, Cake Dough, Noodle Dough, Juice, Meat Dumpling, Pressed Grain, Squeezed Oil, Ground Coffee, Ground Grain, Rice Puffs, Rice Cake, Cooked Rice, Salad, Sashimi, Oil Sauce, Fruit / Veggie Sauce, Sausage, Premium Sausage, Sugar, Fruit Wine.

    The chain Grain → Grain Flour → Bread Dough → Stuffed Bread is unbroken, so properties cooked in at the grain stage can stack all the way to the bread. Tteokbokki and Fried Chicken do not inherit.

    Stays raw: — made from raw meat, it keeps the Raw tag. Type inherited: Grain Flour gets the rice tag if any ingredient is rice (an ingredient of Rice Cake and Tteokbokki).

    #Taste checkLast changed 2026.09.24.5

    When you finish eating, the food's taste is scored and one status effect is applied. Foods that apply a taste effect directly are not judged. EstimatedEstimated

    Score = 20 × Σ (taste value ÷ sensitivity × appetite) appetite multiplies good tastes only Taste value = food data taste formula + tag modifiers (Raw −10 umami, Deep Fried, Stir-fry, umami …) 6+ Phenomenal Flavor · 3+ Delicious · -3 or less Horrible · -6 or less Disgusting
    TasteSensitivity
    Sweet10
    Salty6
    Sour4
    Bitter3
    Greasy10
    Umami(Umami)10
    Astringent6

    Eating the same taste repeatedly wears it out: for a food's dominant tastes (at least 0.8× the strongest taste), appetite drops ×0.8 each time you eat and recovers ×1.25 every 300s (minimum 0.168). Spicy is not judged because the original constants have no sensitivity for it. The original constants (sensitivity, thresholds, ratios) are certain; the score formula is reconstructed from the constant names.

    Phenomenal Flavor
    It's incredibly delicious. You can barely feel your Fatigue. — EXP +5% (300s)
    Delicious
    It's delicious. Your Fatigue is more bearable. — EXP +3% (300s)
    Horrible
    It tastes horrible. Fatigue has increased. — Fatigue gain rate +20% (300s)
    Disgusting
    It tastes vile. Fatigue has increased. — Fatigue gain rate +30% (300s)

    #Dish naming rulesLast changed 2026.09.27.2

    • In-place cooking names apply each recipe's name template to the food's current name. Skewering after stone plate BBQ gives names like “Meat Stone Plate BBQ Skewer”.
    • The first steaming result is named “Steamed [food name]” (no space in Korean). Steaming Sashimi with a Flawless result gives exactly “Well-Made Steamed Sashimi”.
    • Steaming an already steamed food again keeps its name and only increases its properties and the +processing count beside the icon. Legacy “Well-Made Sashimi Steam” names are also preserved.
    • Food burnt by mistake gets a “Burnt” name template and the Burnt property, and a skewer mistake gets the “Undercooked” name.
    • Recipes that create a new food base, like Bread, Cake and Pizza, take the name of the resulting base.

    EstimatedChanged from original (developer decision) Steamed-name spacing, keeping the name on re-steaming, and the + count on icons follow the 2026-09-27 developer instruction and the shared CookingTraitTable/ItemIconWidget rules. The selector below calculates the result name, + count and effects together.
